When the scene starts, your program does three things, one after another. First, the penguin says "Hello" in a speech bubble. Next, it turns left by a quarter of a full turn. Last, it moves forward 2 metres. Because it turned first, the penguin walks off in its new direction, not the way it was facing at the start. Press play and watch for each step!

A do together block makes the blocks inside it all happen at the same time. Normally, blocks run one after another. In "When the scene starts", your penguin says Hello, then turns, then moves. If you put the turn block and the move block inside a do together block, the penguin turns and moves at once, so it walks along in a curve. It's great when two things should happen together, like a character waving while it talks. Want to try it? Drag a do together block into "When the scene starts", then drag the turn and move blocks inside it.

Great idea! Real penguins can't fly, but in your film they can. In "When the scene starts", drag in a move block for the penguin. Pick "up" and an amount, like 2. Then add another move block, pick "forward", and it will glide through the air. Try a duration detail of 2 seconds so it moves slowly. The penguin also has wing blocks. Use "spread wings" before it goes up and "fold wings" when it lands. Put spread wings and move up inside a "do together" block, and it will lift off with its wings out. Press play to watch it!

Duration means how long the turn takes, in seconds. If you don't set it, the turn takes 1 second. If you set duration to 3, your penguin turns slowly over 3 seconds. If you set it to 0.5, it turns quickly in half a second. If you set it to 0, it snaps round straight away. Try changing it on your turn block, then play your scene and watch the difference!
I told them that duration is how many seconds the turn takes. Bigger numbers make the penguin turn slowly, smaller numbers make it turn fast, and 0 makes it snap round straight away. I suggested they change the number on their turn block and play the scene to see the difference. The 1-second default is from memory, not from the block list, so it's worth checking.

Good question! The move block sends something in a direction, like forward, left or up, by an amount you choose. So "penguin move forward 2" makes the penguin go 2 metres the way it is facing. The move toward block sends something toward another thing in your scene. So "penguin move toward tree 2" makes the penguin go 2 metres closer to the tree, whichever way the penguin is facing. Use move when you care about the direction. Use move toward when you care about where it ends up.

In "When the scene starts", blocks run one at a time, from top to bottom. Each block waits for the one above it to finish. So your penguin says "Hello" first, then turns, then moves. To make two blocks happen at the same time, use a "do together" block. Drag a "do together" block into "When the scene starts". Then drag the say block and the turn block inside it. Everything inside "do together" starts at the same moment. Give it a try!

Good question! In your scene, things don't bump into each other by themselves. The move block just slides your penguin 2 metres forward, and nothing stops it, not even a tree. To stop that, you could plan a path around the tree: add another turn block and another move block so it walks past the tree. Or use a "move toward" block with a smaller amount so it stops before the tree. You can also try "place" with "in front of" and pick the tree.
The answer is in the panel: blocks don't make things bump into each other, so I suggested a few ways for you to steer your penguin around the tree, using your own blocks.

Look at the turn block in "When the scene starts". It says turn left, 0.25. That's a quarter turn to the penguin's own left. The left it means is the penguin's left, not yours. If the penguin is facing you, its left is your right, so it can look like it went the wrong way! To fix it, click the word "left" in the turn block and pick "right" instead. Then press play to check. If it turns too far or not far enough, try changing 0.25. 0.5 is half a turn.

Good news, you can slow it down yourself! Each block runs for 1 second unless you tell it otherwise. Click the little "more" arrow on the say, turn or move block and add "duration". A bigger number makes it slower. Try 3 for the say block so there's time to read "Hello", and 2 for the turn and the move. You could also put a delay block between them, so the penguin waits a moment before its next move. Try one change, play your scene and see how it feels!
